_note: The final debate, a month before the election. Three rounds: the opening, the strongest rival's attack, the closing. The attack is picked from your record: a contradiction if there is one, else a group you blamed, else dirty money, else the default. Placeholders: {leader} {party} {rival} {rival_party} {first_date} {first} {second_date} {second} {group}. 'react' (optional) on a line: extra goodwill changes for groups. 'hurt': what an attack that lands costs you before you even answer. Drafts: rewrite freely.

OPENING.title: Opening statement
OPENING.prompt: The moderator turns to {leader}: "Your party didn't exist four years ago. Why should anyone vote for it?"

lines.text: "Because {country} deserves a government that keeps its word. That is all {party} has ever asked for."
"Because for thirty years the people on this stage have robbed you blind, and tonight that ends."
"I'm not a career politician. I'm someone who got tired of waiting for a bus that never comes."
"Look at the people next to me. Would you lend any of them your car?"

attacks.contradiction: "In {first_date} you said: '{first}' In {second_date} you said: '{second}' Which one do you actually believe?"
attacks.blamed: "Your whole campaign has been about blaming {group}. Is that all you have to offer?"
attacks.money: "Where does your party's money come from? Because it isn't from ordinary {nationals}."
attacks.default: "You have never run anything in your life. Why should anyone trust you with a country?"

lines.text: "I have listened and I have learned. A leader who never changes their mind isn't listening."
"How dare you lecture anyone? Your party has lied to this country for a generation."
"At least I change my mind now and then. {rival} hasn't changed a thing since the cassette tape."
"That's invented. Everybody knows your people make things up."

CLOSING.title: Closing statement
CLOSING.prompt: "You have thirty seconds. Speak to the voters."

lines.text: "On election day, vote for the country you want your children to grow up in."
"They are afraid of you. On election day, prove them right."
"If you want more of the same, you know who to vote for. If you don't, you know where to find me."
"If they win again, don't say I didn't warn you."
